summary: STOP-condition premise checked and found FALSE, not assumed. GET /api/v1/events (rest_api_v1.cpp:12389) is the existing in-production precedent: it registers a genuine SSE handler (set_chunked_content_provider, StreamBudget lease, EventBus subscribe) through this exact sink.Get(...) seam, and carries its own TestRouteSink coverage (test_rest_api_events.cpp) whose own file header documents the same boundary this PR's test_legacy_events_routes.cpp now mirrors -- the synchronous handler phase (gate -> admission -> subscribe -> content-provider registration) is fully exercised through TestRouteSink; wire-level chunked SSE framing is deliberately not unit-tested (the #438 TSan trap the sink exists to dodge), covered by UAT/integration instead. HttplibRouteSink::Get forwards byte-identically to httplib::Server::Get in production, so nothing about the registration changes runtime behavior. All 14 routes extracted; 0 deferred.

trigger: the docs test suite's 'plugin readme gate' reddened after adding tests/unit/server/test_diagnostics_routes.cpp
summary: Genuine test-infra regression, not a false alarm: plugin_doc_gen.py's collect_source associates a test file with an agent plugin purely by filename prefix (p.name.startswith(f'test_{name}')), and agents/plugins/{chargen,procfetch,diagnostics}/ are three real, unrelated agent plugins -- the Diagnostics API module this PR extracts happens to dispatch to exactly those two plugin names (forward_legacy_command(req, "chargen", ...) / (req, "procfetch", ...)), so any of the task brief's suggested names (test_diagnostics_routes.cpp, or anything starting test_chargen_*/test_procfetch_*) collides. Fixed by renaming to tests/unit/server/test_legacy_diagnostic_routes.cpp (verified against the full agents/plugins/ listing for further collisions -- none), updating tests/meson.build's comment, and documenting the collision in the file's own header so a future rename attempt doesn't reintroduce it. Re-ran `meson test --suite docs` clean (19 pass, 2 pre-existing unrelated skips) after the fix.

trigger: per-route auth-gate posture must be reproduced exactly, not assumed uniform across the bundle
summary: Confirmed non-uniform, as expected, and reproduced verbatim: Config GET/PUT gate on Infrastructure:Read/Write (PUT additionally calls require_auth AFTER body validation, for audit attribution only); Chargen/Procfetch POSTs gate on Execution:Execute, GETs on Infrastructure:Read; legacy /events gates on deny_service_scoped_session then a NON-blocking resolve_session (never a hard 401 in-handler -- the pre-routing chokepoint is the real auth gate, per the route's own preserved comment); the Instructions fragment gates on deny_service_scoped_session THEN auth_fn with NO perm_fn call, while its sibling yaml-preview route gates on perm_fn(InstructionDefinition,Read) alone; the Approvals fragment gates on auth_fn THEN perm_fn(Approval,Read) (not AuditLog:*, per the pre-existing #3040 rationale preserved in the route's own comment); the MCP-disabled stubs have no gate at all (uniform-disabled response to any caller). Every gate combination is also pinned by a MockHarness test recording the actual (type, op) pairs perm_fn was called with, not an assumed pair.

summary: httplib::Server matches routes by first-match-wins over EXACT strings or std::regex_match (full-string, never partial) in registration order. Checked every route pattern registered by every extracted module ahead of this PR's new insertion point (page_routes, dashboard_api_routes, nvd_routes, custom_properties_routes, result_set_routes) for any pattern that could shadow /events, /api/config(/[a-z_]+)?, /api/chargen/*, /api/procfetch/*, /fragments/instructions(/yaml-preview)?, or /fragments/approvals -- none found (custom_properties_routes' /api/agents/([^/]+)/properties patterns require that literal prefix and cannot match /api/config; no catch-all/prefix-wildcard pattern exists anywhere in this codebase's route registrations). The still-inline routes that come AFTER the new insertion point (health/readiness/etc.) are irrelevant to ordering since they run later regardless. Route order change is therefore behavior-neutral.
